text:
nina.sales: FYI 6 Luminar RFP just landed. Big asks around KMS/HSM, data residency (EU only), and explicit network peering requirements. They also want a POC SOW and a capability matrix. Can SE + Security + Eng triage?

carlos.se: On it. Quick clarifying Q: POC is 4 weeks with 75k docs, embeddings, and "95th < 250ms" for top-level queries. Does that push them to Dedicated or Private?

anya.security: If they mandate FIPS validated HSM for master key material we should plan for Private (on-prem) or Dedicated with customer HSM via partner. Also they want key rotation proof and audit export to their SIEM.

ron.eng: From infra: 75k docs with embeddings + realtime rerank can be satisfied by a 3-node GPU pool with optimized batching; recommend Dedicated reserved commit for consistent perf. Rough committed price ~ $60k/mo, plus snapshot storage and egress. I'll upload the cost sketch.

elena.solutions: I'll assemble the capability matrix and SOW. For the matrix: include rows for "Region pinning", "BYOK/HSM options", "Vector retention policy", "Quantized models supported", "Audit log export", "Peering & Private Link".

nina.sales: Please also include a short legal-safe blurb on liability and SLA credits. Legal asked to cap credits and provide mitigation steps (failover to smaller model, traffic shaping).

legal-bot: Suggested clause: "Vendor liability limited to aggregated service credits not to exceed 12 months of fees for the impacted service; customer may request remediation plan including failover and cross-region fallback."

carlos.se: For KMS copy, propose this snippet:```KMS & HSM Options:
1) Private on-prem: customer HSM, full control, FIPS 140-2/3
2) Dedicated + BYOK: customer CMK provisioned; partner HSM for root wrap
3) Hosted Enterprise: Redwood-managed KMS with customer key import (non-HSM) - audit logs available
Audit export: syslog/S3 push to customer's collector
Rotation: customer-controlled schedule, support windows for rewrap```

anya.security: Add: we must provide key-usage logs (timestamp, operation, principal) and support KMS access reviews. Also add non-disclosure note about model artifacts and vector indexes retained only per contract.

elena.solutions: Uploaded draft attachments: capability_matrix_luminar_v1.xlsx and poc_sow_luminar_draft.docx -> https://drive.redwood/luminar/cm_v1 and https://drive.redwood/luminar/sow_draft

deploy-bot: New file uploaded: "capability_matrix_luminar_v1.xlsx" (owner: elena.solutions)

ron.eng: Peering checklist highlights I'll add to the packet: IP allowlist, private link endpoints, MTU recommendations, test harness for p95 latency, and replay dataset for load tests. See peering-checklist snippet:```- Establish VPC peering / PrivateLink
- Allocate NAT/egress IPs and firewall rules
- Run synthetic load: 10k concurrent queries for 5m windows
- Verify p95 under agreed topology
```

carlos.se: Luminar also asked about vector retention TTL and ability to purge on demand. We should state: "vector retention configurable per-tenant; we support immediate purge requests with verification report."

nina.sales: OK action items: Carlos - finalize KMS snippet + FAQ (EOD). Elena - finalize matrix + SOW (tomorrow 9am). Ron - finalize cost estimate + peering checklist (tomorrow 9am). Anya - security/legal bullets for RFP (tomorrow 10am). I'll consolidate and send. :thumbsup:

anya.security: One blocker to flag back to client: HSM-in-cloud integrations require additional procurement lead time (3-6 weeks) and may impact POC start date. Call that out in the SOW.

elena.solutions: Noted. I'll include timeline options: start with Hosted dev sandbox (no HSM) for initial data prep, then switch to Dedicated/Private when HSM ready.

nina.sales: Thanks team. We'll keep this thread as the canonical pack for Luminar RFP. If Legal needs to join, I'll pull them in.

carlos.se: Uploaded final KMS FAQ draft: https://drive.redwood/luminar/kms_faq_v1.md

ron.eng: Cost sketch uploaded: https://drive.redwood/luminar/dedicated_cost_sketch.pdf

nina.sales: Great. Closing for now; will post when I send the package to Luminar.
